thread.title: Stocks Drop On Apple Downgrade; 2 Retailers Spike | Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Drop On Apple Downgrade; 2 Retailers Spike | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks stepped lower Tuesday as stock market paused after two days of strong gains.
X Apple ( AAPL ) weighed heavily on early action, down almost 2% after an analyst downgrade. Retailers were active on earnings news — RH ( RH ) soared 19%, AutoZone ( AZO ) jumped 5% and Dollar General ( DG ) tumbled nearly 5%. Marijuana stock Cronos Group ( CRON ) bolted 4% higher after confirming it was in early-stage talks with Altria Group ( MO ). Chip stocks were under early pressure, with Intel ( INTC ) down hard among blue chips and Apple supplier Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ) sliding 5% after cutting its third-quarter revenue guidance.
The Dow Jones industrial average dropped 0.4% at the starting bell, with Apple and Intel posting the widest declines.
The S&P 500 futures traded down 0.3%. Autzone rose to the top of the list. Dollar General was the biggest loser among S&P 500 stocks, followed by Pulte Group ( PHM ).
The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.4%, as three of four FANG stocks traded lower and as chipmakers dominated the Nasdaq 100's early declines.
Bond and stock markets will be closed on Wednesday, in observance of memorial services for former President George H.W. Bush.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Dow Jones, S&P 500 Top Midpoints, Nasdaq Stalls The Dow Jones industrials added 1.1% Monday, enough to punch back above the 50-day moving average with some authority. But its last move above that line, in early November, only held for three days. The index is now above the midpoint in its two-month consolidation: 7.1% above its Oct. 29 low, and trading 4.4% below its Oct. 3 peak.
The S&P 500 also gained 1.1% Monday, and broke above its 50-day line for the first time since early October. The benchmark is up 6% from its Oct. 29 low, and 5.3% off its Sept. 21 high.
The Nasdaq Composite racked up a 1.5% advance Monday. That was its sixth gain in the eight sessions since marking a Nov. 20 low, but the move met resistance just as it reached the index's 50-day moving average . The gauge remains well below the midpoint of its consolidation — now 8.9% above the recent low, but still 9.3% from its record high, set in August.
Automakers will report November sales throughout Tuesday's session. New York Federal Reserve Bank President John Williams speaks at 10 a.m. ET in New York.
Oil Prices, China Stock Markets Rise; Japan Dives China's markets managed modest gains Tuesday, buoyed by oil and gas issues. In Japan, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 tumbled 2.4%, hurt by a rising yen and as investors took profits after the market's seven-day advance.
Europe's markets remained under pressure in afternoon trade, with Frankfurt's DAX, the CAC-40 in Paris and London's FTSE 100 all down between 0.4% and 0.6%.
Oil prices continued higher, with West Texas Intermediate paring its early advance to 0.6%, trading just above $53 a barrel. WTI surged almost 4% Monday on trade news and a continued production agreement between Saudi Arabia and Russia. Russia plans to meet along with the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries on Thursday to discuss production quotas. Saudi Energy Minister Khalid Al-Falih early Tuesday walked back some comments regarding production that had stirred optimism. WTI remains down 31% from its Oct. 3 high.
Stocks: Apple, Intel Drag; Cronos Talks To Altria Apple slipped nearly 2% after HSBC downgraded the stock to hold, from buy, while trimming its price target to 200, from 205. The note said the company's revenue growth had become dependent upon price increases, rather than rising unit sales, and that the company was grappling with market saturation. Apple shares are working to add a second week to its rebound off a Nov. 26 low.
Cirrus Logic tumbled 5.4% after cutting its fiscal third-quarter revenue guidance by nearly 20%, to a range of $300 million to $340 million. Cirrus shares are deep in a 17-month consolidation.
Dow Jones stock Intel dropped 2% after Northland Capital Markets downgraded the stock to underperform, from hold. Intel shares have gained in five of the past six weeks, working to climb the right side of a possible five-month base pattern .
Cronos Group jumped 4.9%. The company confirmed it had engaged in early-stage talks with tobacco leader Altria Group "concerning a potential investment" in the company. Cronos shares have climbed for five straight weeks, putting the stock 56% above an early December low.
Earnings News: RH, Dollar General, Toll Brothers, Movado An earnings blowout sent RH, the old Restoration Hardware, up 19% in early trade. The high-end home furnishings retailer is in a two-month base pattern with a possible buy point at 162.20. Shares remained 15% below that buy point .
Autozone rolled ahead 4.1% as its fiscal first-quarter earnings soared past analyst targets, and a 2% revenue gain met expectations. AutoZone stock ended Monday up nearly 14% since clearing a cup-with-handle base in August.
Dollar General surrendered 5.4%, after hurricane and other disaster-related expenses held third-quarter earnings growth to 34%, just below analyst targets. The IBD 50 stock has been sawing its way higher since clearing a cup base in August. Shares ended Monday up 19% so far this year.
Homebuilder stocks moved lower as Toll Brothers ( TOL ) tumbled 10% on the heels of its fiscal fourth-quarter results. Earnings and revenue both cleared analysts' forecasts, but management said demand had weakened in California. Shares have been climbing since late October, attempting to start up the right side of an 11-month consolidation.
Among homebuilding peers, Pulte Group fell almost 5%, DR Horton ( DHI ) dropped 3%.
Watchmaker Movado ( MOV ) popped more than 17% higher. The Paramaus, N.J., horologist reported strong-than-expected third-quarter revenue and earnings growth. The stock reamins deep in a five-month correction.
Hewlett Packard Enterprises ( HPE ) and Marvell Technology ( MRVL ) are scheduled to report after today's closing bell.
